title: "gdalxarray"
subtitle: "An xarray backend powered directly by GDAL"
toc: true
---

```python
import xarray as xr
ds = xr.open_dataset(path_or_uri, engine="gdalxarray")
```

`gdalxarray` is a thin bridge between what GDAL can read (classic
rasters, multidimensional arrays, and every virtual store GDAL knows
about) and xarray's labelled-array model. It is lazy by default,
Dask-chunked on request, and carries CRS and CF time through.

Every code block on this site is run when the site is built, so what
you see is what the current release does against the current GDAL.
The small inputs come from
[wxylib/fixtures](https://github.com/wxylib/fixtures), pinned to one
commit; the larger examples in the [Gallery](gallery/index.qmd) read
public cloud stores, listed with their permanence on the
[Stores](stores.qmd) page.

## A first look

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from _common import *
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

An OISST-shaped Zarr v3 store, written by xarray, opened by GDAL's Zarr
driver and handed to xarray:

```{python}
src = fixture("cf/oisst-like.zarr")
ds = xr.open_dataset(src, engine="gdalxarray")
ds
```

Nothing has been read yet beyond the metadata and the coordinate
arrays. Selecting and plotting pulls only the chunks needed:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "First day of the fixture, read lazily through GDAL's Zarr driver."
sst = ds["sst"].isel(time=0, zlev=0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
sst.plot(ax=ax, cmap="RdYlBu_r", cbar_kwargs={"label": "sst"})
ax.set_title(str(ds.time.values[0])[:10])
plt.show()
```

The same call works for a netCDF on a web server, a COG in a bucket, a
multidimensional VRT, a kerchunk-Parquet reference store or an Icechunk
repository: only the string changes.

```{python}
ds.encoding["gdal_driver"], ds["sst"].encoding.get("preferred_chunks")
```

## Why this exists (and when to use rioxarray instead)

[rioxarray](https://corteva.github.io/rioxarray/) is an accessor and
backend built on [rasterio](https://rasterio.readthedocs.io/). For a
single GeoTIFF or a STAC item it is the mature, well-tested choice.

`gdalxarray` goes straight to `osgeo.gdal`. That matters when:

- **the data is N-dimensional**: GDAL's multidimensional API is exposed
  natively, with named dimensions, not only `(band, y, x)`;
- **the path is a composition**: `/vsicurl/`, `/vsis3/`, `/vsizip/`,
  `vrt://`, `ZARR:`, `NETCDF:`, classic and multidim VRT all nest;
- **driver and codec support should track GDAL**: Zarr v3, kerchunk
  Parquet references, Icechunk, GRIB, HDF4/5 multidim.
